title: Best DevOps Engineers (2026): How to Hire One Safely
description: How to hire a DevOps engineer: what the project should include, how to brief it, cloud costs, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: DevOps engineers set up and automate how your software is built, tested, deployed and run, often on cloud platforms. Good DevOps work makes releases routine and outages rare. It goes wrong when cloud accounts belong to the engineer, costs grow unnoticed, or the setup is so complex nobody else can maintain it. This guide helps you keep control.

faq.q: What does a DevOps engineer do?
faq.a: Typically: automated build and deployment pipelines, cloud infrastructure, monitoring, backups, security settings and scaling. Some also help reduce cloud costs.
It means servers and cloud settings are described in files, such as Terraform, so they can be recreated and reviewed. It makes the setup easier to understand and repeat.

faq.q: How do I keep cloud costs under control?
faq.a: Keep the account in your name, set budget alerts, and ask for an estimate of monthly costs before anything is created. Review the bill after the first month.

faq.q: What access should the engineer have?
faq.a: A dedicated user with only the rights needed, ideally with multi-factor sign-in. Never share the root or owner account.

faq.q: Will my developers understand the setup?
faq.a: Ask for documentation and a handover session. A simpler setup your team understands is often better than an advanced one they cannot maintain.
